event.summary: Removing tmux presence knowledge does not erase unreadable host terminals
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: considered whether removing the unusable-server guard could make Farhelm regard a running but unreadable terminal as absent and discard or duplicate its agent. Source refutation: service/terminals.rs:122-127,225-248 resolves only HostTerminal handles; service/core.rs:6675-6715 keeps unreadable hosts as unattributed handles, and :6743-6755 leaves their durable outcome alone. Startup invokes OldTerminals::end_private_server before reload (:6142-6183); the old-kind row branch is separate (:6675-6679). SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host, The terminal switch points, requires an unreadable host to record nothing durable and refuse lifecycle verbs. The replacement retains that absence/unavailable distinction independently of ServerPresence; no remaining production references to ServerPresence or the removed tmux input/query types were found in the pinned supervisor source. Suggested bucket: highest if that loss/duplication route existed; none established. Could-be-highest: yes, original suspected consequence was loss of or duplicate user processes; refuted for the removal of this guard. Confidence: confirmed by source for the stated replacement distinction, not runtime observation. proposed_drop: source refutation above, not specification acceptance alone. possible_cover: none. Caveats: not a review of all host discovery or lifecycle implementation; the prior release's deliberate ending of old terminals is a separate change and contract.

event.summary: Host lifecycle keeps unavailable terminals and confirms deletion independently of tmux presence
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Original consequence preserved verbatim: removing the unusable-server guard could make Farhelm regard a running but unreadable terminal as absent and discard or duplicate its agent. Original severity retained: could-be-highest, loss of or duplicate user processes. TLDR: the replacement distinguishes unreadable hosts from absent ones, retains host identity at tab close, and propagates an unconfirmed host end before deleting the session row. Initial source refutation remains service/core.rs:6675-6715,6743-6755 and service/terminals.rs:122-127,225-248. Added lifecycle checks: core.rs:13325-13366 refuses an unreadable agent probe and rechecks tab uncertainty after counting; core/host_tabs.rs:1403-1442,1474-1478 requires both session and tab identity at adoption and retains mismatched/unreadable hosts as placeholders. At close, :915-943 requires the exact runtime in the tab cell, refuses the agent runtime and unreadable tabs; :1013-1037 removes the tab/record only on confirmed end, retaining failed endings for retry. session_hosts.rs:771-792 turns all error/missing outcomes into an Err; teardown.rs:531-561 propagates sweep and host-end errors before row removal and :611-651 preserves row/artifacts on failure. Those source checks do not derive later Delete success from the startup retirement's best-effort policy. Governing contracts remain SPEC_impl.md Terminal host, The terminal switch points, Tabs in hosts and Delete ends every terminal host of the session. Suggested bucket: highest if the original process-loss/duplication route existed; none established for deleting ServerPresence. Could-be-highest: yes, unchanged for the caller's independent check. Confidence: source-confirmed for the specified routing, identity and error propagation; no runtime observation. proposed_drop: source refutation, still proposed and not accepted by this reviewer. possible_cover: none. Caveats/provenance: deliberate old-tmux process/screen/history retirement and possible duplication after failed startup termination belong to the prior retirement change, as recorded in the initial event; they are not newly discovered or silently lowered here. This candidate does not rely on their specification acceptance to dismiss a distinct host wrong-target or unconfirmed-Delete route. It is not a review of the complete process-signalling implementation.

event.summary: Qualify host-end confirmation against the Gone runtime shortcut
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Original considered consequence preserved: removing the unusable-server guard could make Farhelm regard a running but unreadable terminal as absent and discard or duplicate its agent; original could-be-highest process-loss/duplication consequence remains. Parent relayed g166/c5:13: an adopted nonplaceholder tab whose runtime reports Gone remains in SessionHosts.tabs and session Delete calls end_launch_host, potentially accepting Gone without verifying the adopted process, whereas end_tab_host performs that verification. TLDR: the previous c1 source evidence establishes propagation of errors that are returned, not that every success establishes process termination. The blanket host-end-confirmation rationale must therefore be qualified. Status: substantive cross-group lead to investigate before a new discovery search, not a confirmed new bug. Next checks: exact end_launch_host/end_tab_host implementations, runtime transitions to Gone, retained host process identity, and in-range attribution. Exact missing premise: a supported shipped route to a Gone runtime while the adopted host process survives and Delete can then forget it. Suggested bucket: highest if this loses access to live user work or leaves credential-bearing processes; no established shipped route yet. Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: unresolved pending source checks; not labelled investigated. proposed_drop: prior source-refutation basis retained only for unreadable-versus-absent distinction, not a blanket Delete guarantee; no drop accepted. possible_cover: g166/c5:13 owns the related investigation. Caveats: source-only; no runtime, fixture substitution or reproduction establishes a production trigger; deliberate old-tmux retirement acceptance does not settle this distinct route.

event.summary: Presence-removal refutation is limited; Gone-runtime Delete shortcut is separately retained
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333; whole range base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a checked for attribution. Original consequence preserved verbatim: removing the unusable-server guard could make Farhelm regard a running but unreadable terminal as absent and discard or duplicate its agent. Original could-be-highest consequence remains loss of or duplicate user processes; no parent drop or lowering is accepted. TLDR: the replacement retains unreadable-versus-absent handling, but my earlier broad all-host-end-confirmation conclusion was too strong. It is corrected here; error propagation cannot prove that a success branch verified termination. Source basis still refutes the narrow removal claim: core.rs:6675-6715,6743-6755 retains unreadable hosts and leaves durable outcomes unchanged, independently of removed ServerPresence. Cross-group reconciliation is now source-checked: session_hosts.rs:245-260 partitions by is_placeholder, which terminal.rs:2091-2097 says describes construction, so an adopted Gone runtime remains among retained tabs and its record is excluded from settlement. session_hosts.rs:733-740 calls end_launch_host directly; host_launch.rs:694-696 accepts Err(Gone) without adopted-process verification. terminal.rs:2374-2385 returns final liveness for an ended runtime. Close does have an extra adopted-process check at host_tabs.rs:1056-1062. session_hosts.rs:510-521 checks only the child's root; terminal.rs:771-784 may yield none after the child exits, independently of host-process survival. The retained close test at core/tests/host_terminals.rs:3685-3780 explicitly removes the socket and disconnects a stand-in, retaining its adopted live process; it proves the semantic distinction, not an ordinary real-host occurrence or that Delete itself removes the socket. Known g166/c5 records this conditional orphan-host consequence. It is not dismissed here and is not new discovery by g168. No user-process/data-loss consequence for that distinct orphan-host route is established here; the original potential-highest wrong absence/duplication concern above is preserved separately. Attribution check: the exclusive range base already contains host_launch.rs:684's Gone-success shortcut and session_hosts.rs:751's direct tab call. git log -G for those exact branches over the complete base-to-tip range returns no changes. Thus deleting presence.rs neither introduced this shortcut nor repaired it; this is not merely an immediate-parent comparison. Suggested bucket: highest if the original loss/duplication route existed; no route attributable to this removal established. Confidence: source-confirmed for the narrow model replacement and the separately known shortcut; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation only of the removal's unreadable-host regression claim, still proposed; expressly not a proposed drop of g166/c5 or a blanket assertion that Delete always confirms host death. possible_cover: g166/c5 owns the independently retained conditional Gone-runtime issue. Caveats: supported occurrence of socket disappearance plus runtime loss is not established by the test's manual fixture; the conditional branch defect and its process-confirmation contract remain valid cross-group evidence without reproducing it. Known startup retirement/failed-termination duplication has separate earlier-change provenance, and its acceptance is not used to settle this route. c1's temporary cross-group source lead is resolved; no readily checkable premise remains in g168's assigned removal claim.

event.summary: Input confirmation remains in the host attachment path
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: considered whether deleting the dedicated confirmed-input client silently loses typed input during a host connection failure or takeover. Source refutation: service/grid_stream.rs:1022-1036 gives each attachment a host InputSequence and pump; :1244-1275 retains and awaits every input receipt; :1209-1238 publishes input failure; :1285-1294 reports Unknown and NotSent instead of accepting them as successful delivery. This path resolves a HostTerminal (service/terminals.rs:122-127,225-248), so it does not fall back to an unconfirmed tmux pipe write. Contract: SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host, Grid streams, says input whose fate is unknown or not sent ends the attachment as an input failure; runtime input is never resent. Suggested bucket: high for lost interactive input if the route existed. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from this deletion; the considered consequence was silently dropped keystrokes. Confidence: confirmed by source for the attachment-to-receipt path, not runtime observation. proposed_drop: source refutation above. possible_cover: none. Caveats: handing input to the runtime is asynchronous; this is not a claim that a queued key has already been read by the agent. A connection loss is explicitly allowed to leave delivery unknown, and no runtime was exercised.

event.summary: Input confirmation remains in the host attachment and prompt paths
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Original considered consequence preserved: deleting the dedicated confirmed-input client silently loses typed input during a host connection failure or takeover. TLDR: the host attachment retains receipt/failure handling; the non-viewer prompt caller also checks delivery before submitting. Initial source basis retained: service/grid_stream.rs:1022-1036,1209-1238,1244-1294 uses an InputSequence, awaits receipts and reports Unknown/NotSent. Synthesis checks: service/core.rs:11913-11959 holds the session lifecycle claim while resolving and probing the exact session entry, :11978-12010 requires caught-up bracketed-paste modes, and :2192-2225 waits for InputFate::Written for the whole paste before sending submit through the same sequence, with a whole-operation timeout and partial-delivery errors. connection.rs's patch preserves the attachments-lock check of both channel and notify identity when routing input (:501 onward in the new revision); it changes the host branch from backend dispatch to direct HostAttach dispatch rather than removing identity validation. The deleted input tests proved the retired tmux client's whole-call timeout and confirmed chunks, not a generic host-runtime deadline. Surviving test code service/grid_stream/tests.rs:1014-1044 asserts received key/paste bytes; :1113-1146 fills the actual runtime input window with three held pieces before injecting query output and another producer, then asserts the entire received sequence. Thus the test check relies on actual competing bytes and fixture premises, not merely correct production code. Contract: SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host, Grid streams and The terminal switch points, requires failed unknown/not-sent input to break the attachment and a prompt to submit only after its whole paste is written. Suggested bucket: high for silently lost interactive input if the route existed. Could-be-highest: no established security or user-owned-work loss route from this deletion; original silent-keystroke consequence is unchanged. Confidence: source-confirmed for the stated paths and test assertions; no execution observation. proposed_drop: source refutation, still proposed and not accepted by this reviewer. possible_cover: none. Caveats: queued input is not proof of agent consumption; delivery can become unknown after disconnect. Accepted interleaving between a completed prompt paste and its separate submit is not being used to dismiss a distinct deletion bug. No assertion of complete host test coverage or mutation-test execution.

event.summary: Removing tmux query stripping does not expose queries to a second terminal parser
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: considered whether deleting QueryStripper brings back duplicate cursor/color replies that appear as spurious shell input. Source refutation: the deleted transform applied to tmux raw control-mode output. event.summary: Retiring stdin-only tmux input does not move typed credentials into process arguments
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: checked the deleted input client's explicit privacy responsibility: typed input can contain credentials, so replacing it must not put those bytes on a spawned process command line. The replacement sends input as binary host-protocol payload, with no process invocation on this path. Details: the removed InputClient documentation at original input.rs:89 onward identifies argv exposure as the reason old send-keys invocations were avoided. At the reviewed revision hosts/terminal.rs:1527-1534,1552-1575,2300-2338 queues byte vectors in the host runtime and stamps the input epoch; hosts/client.rs:852-863 encodes ClientMessage::Input(data.to_vec()) into the established connection after bounded admission. This is not shell/tmux command interpolation. The grid-input encoder at grid_input.rs:177 converts text directly to UTF-8 bytes, and input_frames at :267-272 cuts those bytes at MAX_INPUT for the same protocol, rather than constructing process arguments. Governing contract: SPEC_impl.md, The grid client, states input is encoded by the supervisor from the terminal modes; Terminal host, A host terminal's runtime, sends input through the owned host connection. Suggested bucket: highest if typed credentials were exposed through process arguments. Could-be-highest: yes; original considered consequence here is disclosure of credential-bearing typed input to readers of process arguments. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of that removed-client replacement route; no execution or exposure observed. proposed_drop: source refutation above, pending independent check; no drop accepted. possible_cover: none. Caveats: this is limited to the input-delivery transport and does not claim arbitrary agent commands or the user's terminal program never expose secrets themselves. It is a considered non-finding discovered during the privacy/responsibility audit, not a new verified vulnerability. Original c2 silent-input-loss consequence and its source/test records remain separate and unchanged.
